skills.name: Analyze-Tests
skills.description: Use before starting the Build workflow to generate a comprehensive test strategy and verification plan.

skills.name: architecture
skills.description: Architectural decision-making framework. Requirements analysis, trade-off evaluation, ADR documentation. Use when making architecture decisions or analyzing system design.

skills.name: Brain-Dump-to-Epics
skills.description: Use this skill when the user asks to transform unstructured thoughts and ideas into structured Product Epics.

skills.name: Code-Review
skills.description: Use after implementing code to run a two-stage review — spec compliance first, then code quality. Order matters.

skills.name: Handoff
skills.description: Compact the current conversation into a self-contained handoff document a fresh agent or later session can pick up cleanly. Use when context is getting long (approaching the ~120k-token smart zone), moving from planning to doing, or passing work between loop iterations.

skills.name: Collaborative-Drafting
skills.description: The drafting primitive. When a workflow must produce a structured document (Epics, screens, implementation slices, an architecture), lead with a complete draft the human corrects — never a blank-page questionnaire. Reach for it in Grand PRD, UX/UI Brief, Technical Vision, Carve, and any 'propose then refine' phase.

skills.name: Context-Engineering
skills.description: Use when updating the task backlog, reading PRDs, or modifying project state in the conductor/ directory

skills.name: Context-Updater
skills.description: Use after Build or Retrospective to update Product Area and Context files with what was learned and built.

skills.name: Domain-Modeling
skills.description: Use when establishing or refining the shared vocabulary of the product — during Technical Vision, when naming entities or slices in Carve, when writing a spec, or any time a term is ambiguous or two people mean different things by the same word. Turns the static glossary into a living ubiquitous-language discipline.

skills.name: frontend-design
skills.description: Design thinking and decision-making for web UI. Use when designing components, layouts, color schemes, typography, or creating aesthetic interfaces. Teaches principles, not fixed values.

skills.name: GitHub-CLI
skills.description: GitHub workflow using the gh CLI — issues, PRs, releases, and Actions. Use when the project is hosted on GitHub. Conventions (commit/branch/PR-body) come from git-workflow.

skills.name: GitLab-CLI
skills.description: GitLab workflow using the glab CLI — issues, MRs, wiki, and CI/CD. Use when the project is hosted on GitLab. Conventions (commit/branch/MR-body) come from git-workflow.

skills.name: Git-Workflow
skills.description: Core git workflow conventions — commit messages, branch naming, PR/MR descriptions. Use whenever committing, branching, or creating pull/merge requests.

skills.name: using-git-worktrees
skills.description: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - creates isolated git worktrees with smart directory selection and safety verification

skills.name: Grilling
skills.description: The interview primitive. A relentless, one-question-at-a-time interview that sharpens a plan, design, or idea before any building begins. Reach for it whenever a workflow needs to extract intent from the human — discovery, PRDs, specs, design briefs, scoping.

skills.name: Independent-Review
skills.description: The fresh-context review gate — when a workflow produces a consequential artifact (PRD, architecture, spec, carved plan, diff), a separate reviewer that did not produce it decides whether it's ready before it's saved or handed off. The Maker/Checker split applied to any artifact; loaded by the blueprint workflows and Ship.

skills.name: Judge-Panel
skills.description: The divergent-then-convergent decision primitive — when a decision has a wide, hard-to-reverse solution space (an architecture, a hard design/algorithm choice), generate N candidates from different angles, score them with independent judges, then synthesize the winner while grafting the best of the runners-up. Opt-in; loaded by Technical Vision.

skills.name: Writing-Evals
skills.description: How to write an evalset for the app's non-deterministic surface — LLM-calling features whose output a unit test can't pin down. The Eval-Driven Law's how-to (the pre-commit gate requires an eval alongside provider-calling code). Three grading modes: rubric/LM-judge, property/assertion, reference. Loaded by Build when a task touches LLM-feature code.

skills.name: Architecture-Checklist
skills.description: Turn 'follow the architecture' into explicit checkable items. Technical-Vision/Carve write a machine-readable compliance checklist (conductor/0-compass/architecture-checklist.md) from the architecture decisions; the Checker (loop + independent-review) verifies the diff against each item — deterministic (a `check:` shell command) or semantic. The semantic half of the ship-contract; the Eval-Driven Law is the deterministic half.

skills.name: i18n-localization
skills.description: Internationalization and localization patterns. Detecting hardcoded strings, managing translations, locale files, RTL support.

skills.name: lint-and-validate
skills.description: Automatic quality control, linting, and static analysis procedures. Use after every code modification to ensure syntax correctness and project standards. Triggers onKeywords: lint, format, check, validate, types, static analysis.

skills.name: Model-Routing
skills.description: Use when deciding which model tier to run a task, subagent, or loop role on — match model capability and reasoning effort to task difficulty instead of defaulting to one model for everything. Reach for it when spinning up scouts/Checkers, configuring the autonomous loop, or when a task is either trivially mechanical or unusually hard.

skills.name: Skill-Registry
skills.description: Manages Conductor skills from the remote registry — install, remove, search, and list skills using the conductor CLI. Use during Technical Vision workflow or whenever the tech stack changes.

skills.name: Subagent-Isolation
skills.description: Use when a task needs reading across many files, several independent investigations, or long unbounded exploration — delegate to scout subagents so the main context stays clean and under budget. Also the pattern for parallel work that must not collide. Isolation is the default, not an optimization.

skills.name: System-Janitor
skills.description: Use this skill when the user asks to scan the Conductor Framework for misplaced files and recommend reorganization.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.description: 4-phase systematic debugging methodology with root cause analysis and evidence-based verification. Use when debugging complex issues.

skills.name: Task-Tracker
skills.description: Use during Build workflow execution to maintain a live task tracker. Update at every state change.

skills.name: Trace-Documentation
skills.description: Use to generate or update trace.md files that link project backlog items directly to code modifications.

skills.name: UX-Reviewer
skills.description: Use this skill when the user asks to review designs and provide UX feedback and suggestions.

skills.name: Verification-Gate
skills.description: Use this skill when about to claim any work is done. Enforces the Verification Iron Law — evidence before assertions, always.

skills.name: Behavior-Validator
skills.description: Source-blind, black-box validation of the running artifact. A validator that has NOT read the implementation exercises the live app/CLI/API as a real operator, with adversarial anti-cheat probes, and reports observed behavior against a contract. Dynamic complement to verification-gate and independent-review.

rules.name: loop-guardrails
rules.description: Loop-scoped safety limits (iteration ceiling, anti-stall, evidence rule). Loaded by the unattended-loop workflow — NOT always-on. Interactive sessions don't pay for it.

rules.name: prime-directive
rules.description: Context First. Plan Second. Build Third.

rules.name: test-driven-law
rules.description: Red before green. No implementation code without a failing test first.

rules.name: verification-iron-law
rules.description: No completion claims without fresh verification evidence.

workflows.name: deepen
workflows.description: Deepen (Brownfield Architecture Improvement) — find shallow/scattered modules in an existing codebase and reshape them into deep modules with narrow interfaces, safely. Driven by the Code Archaeologist.

workflows.name: loop-checker
workflows.description: The independent Checker's audit brief, run as a SEPARATE process each loop beat: adopt the Checker persona, judge the diff against goal_description plus the architecture checklist, and record a fail-safe verdict to checker-verdict.json. The driver treats a missing or malformed verdict as a rejection.

workflows.name: TDD-Cycle
workflows.description: Use during execution to enforce the strict RED → GREEN → REFACTOR test-driven development loop.

workflows.name: unattended-loop
workflows.description: The autonomous loop's agent-side workflow: the per-beat judgment the deterministic `conductor loop` driver delegates. Reads loop-state.json, applies the Scoping Barrier and trigger-trust checks, loads the phase-appropriate persona, and does one beat of work. The driver owns every counter, gate and merge.

workflows.name: ux-ui-design-brief
workflows.description: UX/UI Design Brief (Translating Epics into Interface)
